'''Damien Lamont Wilkins''' (born January 11, 1980)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Damien Wilkins Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/wilkida02.html|access-date=2020-11-08|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and basketball executive who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] for ten seasons. He is the son of retired 13-year NBA veteran [[Gerald Wilkins]] and nephew of nine-time NBA All-Star, Hall of famer [[Dominique Wilkins]].

==College career==
After graduating from [[Dr. Phillips High School]] in [[Orlando, Florida]], Wilkins enrolled at [[North Carolina State University]]. Two years into a quick and promising start to his NCAA career at North Carolina State, Wilkins entered the [[2001 NBA draft]] but decided to withdraw and transfer to [[University of Georgia]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Cole|first=Bill|title=Wilkins is expected to make choice on Tuesday|url=http://www.journalnow.com/wsj/sports/basketball/college/MGB1WBP92OC.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20010702051156/http://www.journalnow.com/wsj/sports/basketball/college/MGB1WBP92OC.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 2, 2001|newspaper=Winston-Salem Journal|date=June 17, 2001|access-date=March 24, 2005}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dickvitale/vpreview021031toptransfers.html|title=Georgia's Wilkins leads list of five best transfers|work=ESPN.com|date=October 31, 2002|access-date=March 24, 2005}}</ref> There, he had two solid but unspectacular seasons and went undrafted in 2004.

==Professional career==
Diligence in the weight room helped Wilkins have a big summer league and shine in preseason action for the Sonics, allowing him to make the team. Working after practice, Wilkins got his shot towards the end of his rookie season and scored 21 points at Portland on March 24, 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=250324022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050404054505/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=250324022|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 4, 2005|title=Seattle withstands Blazers' final-period rally|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2005|access-date=March 24, 2005}}</ref> Wilkins would start seven games the rest of the way as the Sonics battled injuries. He proved himself in the [[2005 NBA Playoffs|2005 Playoffs]] when injuries struck again, finishing with 15 points, six rebounds and five steals in the Sonics' Game 4 win over San Antonio.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=250515025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060223004248/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=250515025|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 23, 2006|title=With Lewis sidelined, Allen shoulders load with 32 points|work=ESPN.com|date=May 16, 2005|access-date=May 16, 2005}}</ref> A restricted free agent in the summer of 2005, Wilkins received an offer from the Minnesota Timberwolves in August 2005,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2137777|title=Wilkins gets offer sheet from Wolves|work=ESPN.com|date=August 18, 2005|access-date=August 18, 2005}}</ref> which the Sonics matched within 7 days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2142183|title=Wilkins to stay with Sonics|work=ESPN.com|date=August 24, 2005|access-date=August 24, 2005}}</ref>

[[File:WilkinsLayup.jpg|thumb|Wilkins playing for the Sonics.]]
In the 2007 season, the departure of [[Rashard Lewis]] and [[Ray Allen]] made Wilkins a starter. On November 16, 2007, he scored a career-high 41 points and grabbed 9 rebounds in a game against the Atlanta Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271116001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071119145110/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271116001|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 19, 2007|title=Wilkins scores 41, but Durant's 3-pointer clinches Sonics' double-OT win|work=ESPN.com|date=November 17, 2007|access-date=November 17, 2007}}</ref>

On July 27, 2009, Wilkins was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] along with [[Chucky Atkins]] for center [[Etan Thomas]] and two future second-round draft picks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Minnesota_Acquires_Damien_Wilk-090727.html|title=Minnesota Acquires Wilkins and Atkins from Thunder|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2009|access-date=July 27, 2009}}</ref>

On September 28, 2010, he was signed by the Memphis Grizzlies, but he was waived at the end of training camp on October 21.

On December 3, 2010, he signed a contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] after [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]]'s injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Damien_Wilkins_PR_120310.html|title=HAWKS SIGN SWINGMAN DAMIEN WILKINS|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2010|access-date=December 4, 2010}}</ref> The Hawks released him after one month.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2011-01-05-803583893_x.htm|title=Hawks release backup Damien Wilkins|date=January 5, 2011|work=USAToday.com|access-date=January 5, 2011}}</ref>

On January 8, 2011, the Atlanta Hawks signed Wilkins to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Damien_Wilkins_PR_010811.html|title=HAWKS SIGN DAMIEN WILKINS TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|work=NBA.com|date=January 8, 2011|access-date=January 8, 2011}}</ref> On January 28, 2011, the Hawks signed him for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Damien_Wilkins_PR_012811.html|title=HAWKS SIGN DAMIEN WILKINS FOR REMAINDER OF THE SEASON|work=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2011|access-date=January 28, 2011}}</ref>

During the 2011–12 season, Wilkins played for the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/89187/detroit-pistons-announce-damien-wilkins.html|title=Detroit Pistons announce Damien Wilkins|date=December 10, 2011|work=Sportando.com|access-date=December 10, 2011}}</ref> In September 2012, he signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-2012-training-camp-roster|title=Sixers Announce 2012 Training Camp Roster|date=September 27, 2012|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 27, 2012}}</ref>

On September 30, 2013, he rejoined the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14381|title=Atlanta Hawks fill up their training camp roster|date=September 30, 2013|work=InsideHoops.com|access-date=September 30, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015214846/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14381|archive-date=October 15, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 14, 2013, he was waived by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14531|title=Atlanta Hawks waive David Lighty, Adonis Thomas, Damien Wilkins|date=October 14, 2013|work=InsideHoops.com|access-date=October 14, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014212811/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14531|archive-date=October 14, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In December 2013, he signed with the Beijing Ducks of China.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/230910/Damien-Wilkins-Signing-With-Beijing-Ducks-Of-Chinal|title=Damien Wilkins Signing With Beijing Ducks Of China|date=December 1, 2013|work=RealGM.com|access-date=December 1, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/108780/damien-wilkins-agreed-to-terms-with-beijing.html|title=Damien Wilkins agreed to terms with Beijing|date=December 1, 2013|work=Sportando.com|access-date=December 1, 2013}}</ref> In his first game for the Ducks, he recorded 10 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 assist in a 106–99 victory over Liaoning.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2013/1206_1944_941.asp?|title=Regular Season Round 10: Liaoning H. – Beijing Ducks 99–106|date=December 6, 2013|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=December 6, 2013}}</ref>

On May 1, 2014, he signed with [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] for the rest of the 2014 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/118677/damien-wilkins-signs-with-indios-de-mayaguez.html|title=Damien Wilkins signs with Indios de Mayaguez|date=May 1, 2014|work=Sportando.com|access-date=May 1, 2014}}</ref>

On November 1, 2014, he was selected by the [[Iowa Energy]] with the 16th overall pick in the 2014 [[NBA Development League]] draft.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/20142015_energy_training_camp_2014_11_02.html|title=IOWA ENERGY FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|date=November 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 1, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610055838/http://www.nba.com/dleague/iowa/20142015_energy_training_camp_2014_11_02.html|archive-date=June 10, 2016}}</ref> On February 4, 2015, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2015 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|title=Thirteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented by Kumho Tire|date=February 15, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 27, 2015|archive-date=February 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150205023335/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters-2015/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On April 20, he returned to Indios de Mayagüez.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/158883/damien-wilkins-back-to-indios-de-mayaguez.html|title=Damien Wilkins back to Indios de Mayaguez|work=Sportando.com|date=April 20, 2015|access-date=April 20, 2015}}</ref>

After initially signing with a Venezuelan team for the 2015–16 season, Wilkins was swayed into re-entering the NBA following the injury to [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]] of the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. He and his agent contacted the Hornets and the two parties came to an agreement on a non-guaranteed training camp contract on October 5, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/damien-wilkins-credits-the-luck-of-endlessly-delayed-flights-for-his-new-hornets-deal-224352204.html|title=Damien Wilkins credits the luck of delayed flights for his new Hornets deal|work=Sports.Yahoo.com|date=October 5, 2015|access-date=October 5, 2015}}</ref> On October 16, he officially signed with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-sign-damien-wilkins|title=Hornets Sign Damien Wilkins|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 16, 2015|access-date=October 16, 2015}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Hornets a week later after appearing in three preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/clone-charlotte-hornets-add-thompson-and-washburn-training-camp-roster|title=Hornets Waive Four Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2015|access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref> Two days later, he signed with [[Guaros de Lara (basketball)|Guaros de Lara]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|Venezuelan League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/179871/damien-wilkins-signs-with-guaros-de-lara.html|title=Damien Wilkins signs with Guaros de Lara|work=Sportando.com|date=October 25, 2015|access-date=October 25, 2015}}</ref>

On October 31, 2016, Wilkins was acquired by the [[Greensboro Swarm]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://greensboro.dleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-announce-2016-training-camp-roster/|title=Greensboro Swarm Announce 2016 Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2016|access-date=November 20, 2016}}</ref>

In April 2017, Wilkins joined [[Brujos de Guayama]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/231654/damien-wilkins-signs-with-brujos-de-guayama.html Damien Wilkins signs with Brujos de Guayama]</ref>

On August 15, 2017, Wilkins signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]], returning to the NBA for the first time since 2013.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-damien-wilkins-and-ben-moore Pacers Sign Damien Wilkins and Ben Moore]</ref> On January 7, 2018, Wilkins was waived by the Pacers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-request-waivers-wilkins Pacers Request Waivers on Wilkins]</ref> On February 1, 2018, Wilkins returned to [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/damien-wilkins-returns-swarm/|title=Damien Wilkins Returns To Swarm|work=NBA.com|date=February 1, 2018|access-date=February 1, 2018}}</ref>

==National team career==
Wilkins represented the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]], where he won a bronze medal.

==Personal life==
Wilkins is the son of retired 13-year NBA veteran [[Gerald Wilkins]] and nephew of nine-time NBA All-Star [[Dominique Wilkins]]. [[Isaiah Wilkins]], the stepson of [[Dominique Wilkins|Dominique]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Virginia's Isaiah Wilkins, stepson of NBA legend Dominique Wilkins, forges his own path |url=http://dailyorange.com/2016/01/virginias-isaiah-wilkins-stepson-of-nba-legend-dominique-wilkins-forges-his-own-path/ |website=Daily Orange |access-date=July 22, 2018 |date=July 22, 2018}}</ref> also played basketball professionally.<ref>{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Jaylen Barford, Zach Smith and Isaiah Wilkins To Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-jaylen-barford-zach-smith-and-isaiah-wilkins-training-camp|date=July 26, 2018|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 26, 2018}}</ref>

Wilkins has been the General Manager and Head of Basketball of [[Overtime Elite]] since September 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Lauren |title=Overtime Elite's Damien Wilkins adding to family legacy |language=English |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/damien-wilkins-adds-to-family-legacy-as-head-of-overtime-elite/S6SCL66G6ZBINDHB2VJHK5TOIQ/ |access-date=2022-09-23 |issn=1539-7459}}</ref>
